source.author: Hugo Duminil-Copin
source.title: Lectures on the Ising and Potts models on the hypercubic lattice
source.locator: Conjecture 6, printed p. 94 (PDF p. 93); definition (7.1), preceding page; Exercise 34 and Exercise 61(1)
source.short_quote: If g(beta) tends to 0 as beta tends to beta_c, the field is said to be trivial.
source.exact_operational_target: For nearest-neighbor zero-field Ising on Z^3 at beta<beta_c, with chi(beta)=sum_x <sigma_0 sigma_x>_beta, xi(beta) the inverse exponential decay rate along e_1, and U4 the connected four-spin correlation, g(beta)=[sum_{x2,x3,x4} U4(0,x2,x3,x4)]/[chi(beta)^2 xi(beta)^3]. Show g(beta) does not tend to zero as beta increases to beta_c.
source.sign_note: U4 is nonpositive by the source's Lebowitz inequality, so g is nonpositive. A positive lower bound concerns -g, not g.
source.relationship_to_field_limit: The source motivates g through Gaussian Wick factorization but its stated definition of nontriviality is the beta-to-beta_c coupling criterion. Existence and non-Gaussianity of a full critical scaling-field limit are not separately established by this definition.
